title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure at the configuration layer of a developer tool, not a model producing wrong output. A codebase indexing feature shipped enabled by default, and developers reported that it sent their local repositories to a cloud service without their permission. The failure sits in the gap between what the tool did by default and what its users understood it to do, and it ran silently inside a workflow where developers had already granted the assistant access to their source code.

Catching it before release would have required someone to review the default state of every feature that touches the network, rather than only the features users opt into. A permission prompt at first run, or monitoring of outbound traffic from the client, would have surfaced the uploads earlier. The company's response, turning the feature off and then closing the upload route, addresses the transmission but not the default that produced it.

What is not established is whether any code data was retained. Z.ai said independent reviews found none, and a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded was withdrawn by the party that made it. The reports of unauthorised uploads come from developers, and no finding of intent has been reported.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Developers said Z.ai's ZCode AI coding assistant sent local code repositories to Alibaba Cloud without permission. Z.ai blamed a Codebase Indexing feature that was on by default, apologized, fixed the flaw, and then closed the upload route. A company withdrew a separate claim that six workspaces with sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai stated that independent reviews found no code data had been kept.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
